source.title: Unlocking the Address Book: Dissecting the Sparse Semantic Structure of LLM Key-Value Caches via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Qing-Sen Ma; Dian-Yun Wang; J. Lyu; Yaoye Wang; Lechen Ning; Sujie Zhu; Zhenbo Xu; Liu-Yu Xiang; Hui-Ning Li; Hui-Jia Wu; Zhao-Feng He

record.file_problem: The supplied text begins mid-sentence in the abstract, and refers to Table 4 without including it. The paper is otherwise identifiable and includes the main sections and references.
record.tranche_reason: Applies Top-K SAEs to LLM key and value caches and reports reconstruction and performance results, extending sparse-feature analysis to this setting rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstruction-fidelity results and qualitative feature activations, which bear on V4. Its end-to-end PPL and zero-shot results are recorded under fits_no_version because they show the effects of SAE-compressed attention, not directly whether features are sparse or recoverable. Background results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains Top-K SAEs on Key/Value projections of several LLMs. It reports how well a sparse dictionary reconstructs those vectors (cosine similarity vs. budget K) and inspects feature activations. This bears on V4's 'sparse features a dictionary can recover' in a new setting, the KV cache. The evidence is weak. Sparsity is imposed by Top-K. Fidelity is given with no comparison such as PCA at the same rank, a random dictionary or a shuffled control. The feature examples are anecdotal, from 10 probe sentences. The main aim is KV compression, so this sits near T4, but the fidelity curves and the Key/Value contrast are results on recoverability.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Additions: the authors claim Top-8 truncation often improves PPL (a 'Denoising Hypothesis', with ranks 9+ treated as noise). They also say the SAE 'deconstructs the superposition' of polysemous words like 'bank' into orthogonal features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Top-K SAEs trained on LLM KV projections and measures reconstruction fidelity, feature activations, and downstream compression performance; it does not use the original toy-model setup or its feature-sparsity/importance sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and representation type matter: shallow Values are more compressible than deep Values, and deep Values benefit from K=16 rather than K=8.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing KV vectors with Top-K SAE reconstructions leaves wikitext-2 PPL and zero-shot accuracy near the dense baseline. K=8 PPL is slightly lower than dense in all four models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-dictionary reconstructions of KV caches preserve downstream LM performance (a compression/'denoising' claim).

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report qualitative layer-wise roles of Key features: lexical n-gram features at L2, syntactic 'backbone' features at L16, polysemy-resolving features at L30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional stratification of SAE features across attention depth.

record.problems: The supplied text omits the referenced Table 4 and begins mid-abstract. Some reconstruction results are described qualitatively or are figure-only; no uncertainty estimates are supplied. The accuracy table reports five scores although its legend names six benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no phase transition and no geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or of importance-based allocation of dimensions.
No analysis of other causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons. No residual-stream or MLP analysis. No baseline (PCA or random dictionary) to show the structure is sparse and not merely low-rank.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or canonicality of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: To match the L2 Value fidelity at K=8 (~0.86), Yi-6B L30 Values need nearly K=32.
Middle-layer syntactic Key features: Feature 3012/2430 activations on function words across domains (e.g., 10.62, 11.50). Layer-2 Feature 3655 on 'of'/'Paris'.
Table 4 (K=8 vs K=16 vs K=128 performance) is referenced but absent from the text. Qwen2.5-32B results claimed in the abstract are not reported.

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies: Sec. 4.3 gives Key cosine ≈0.81 at K=8, while the Fig. 4 caption says >0.86. The text claims K=16 yields lower PPL than K=8 'as seen in Table 3', but Table 3 has no K=16 column, and K=8 has lower PPL than K=32 throughout. Sec. 5.1 says SAEs were trained on Key projections only, yet Value results are reported. The Table 3 legend names six benchmarks but five scores are given. There is no uncertainty and no control baseline (PCA or a random dictionary), so reconstruction fidelity does not distinguish sparse dictionary structure from low-rank structure. Support for V4 is therefore weak.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for capacity, including the allocation of dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Does not measure features spread across neurons; SAE results concern KV projections, not a general account of LLM representations.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs or settings, or canonical units of the model.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional underlying features in the model.

relationships.condition: Key vectors (Yi-6B L16/L30, Mistral-7B L30) and shallow Values (Yi-6B L2), at K=8
relationships.reason: 8 of 4096 dictionary latents recover about 0.81–0.86 cosine (R1, R2, R3, R8). Context-specific Key features appear in anecdotal probes (R10, R11). There is no control baseline.
relationships.display_finding: Eight active latents out of 4,096 recovered about 0.81–0.86 cosine similarity, and anecdotal probes showed context-specific Key features. There is no control baseline.

tranche.reason: The study examines sparse dictionary recoverability and semantic feature activations in a new setting, LLM Key-Value projections, beyond reporting compression performance alone.

source_check.notes: Sec. 5.1 specifies Key-only SAE training despite reporting Value results; Value training and the Qwen setup are underspecified. R10–R11 concern different tokens in two sentences and provide anecdotal evidence, without controlled feature-specificity or orthogonality tests.

reader_labels.reason: The Top-K dictionary recovers substantial Key directionality and yields context-specific activations in the examples (R1, R2, R8, R10, R11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Shallow Values reconstruct well at K=8, but deep Yi-6B and Mistral Values are less sparse at K=8 and improve with a larger budget (R3-R7, R9).
